output.summary: The NRR drop is mostly lost expansion (-12.3 of -16 pts), not churn. The price increase and Routewise are poor explanations. Price-locked accounts fell as much as accounts that got the increase. The price-reason churn coding is biased by a default dropdown value. Routewise took only 6 logos ($0.41M), all in North America, while EMEA shows the same pattern and Routewise doesn't sell there. The implementation cut plausibly caused the longer queue (16 to 67 days). Expansion stalling then followed, but the migration reliability decline is confounded with it, and the customer account says both mattered. Wave-level and queue-level data would separate them. Run the cheap record analysis and a randomized partner-capacity test. Do not roll back pricing, freeze the roadmap or rehire permanently yet.
